title: Offensive Edge / False-Negative Opportunity Cost
question: How much upside has the framework sacrificed through delayed confirmation, by asset tier and regime, and when was that delay justified by drawdown avoided?
hypothesis: The framework's defensive stack has genuine protection value but may impose materially different false-negative costs across BTC, ETH and alt tiers; a uniform confirmation posture may not be economically optimal.
baseline: Existing FNP, deployment, forecast/sequence and decision lineage evaluated point-in-time without hindsight entry selection.
required_analysis: Reconstruct comparable decision episodes and preserve frozen horizons.
Compare WAIT/permission/actual action against preregistered or mechanically defined partial-deployment counterfactuals.
Segment BTC, ETH, large, mid and small/micro where evidence supports it.
Quantify delay days, upside missed, drawdown avoided and net decision divergence.
Distinguish justified caution from excess confirmation cost.
Test whether false-negative cost is regime-dependent and tier-dependent.
falsifier: Apparent offensive underperformance disappears after point-in-time constraints, reasonable baseline choice and drawdown-risk adjustment.
kill_condition: If opportunity-cost estimates are unstable, hindsight-dependent or do not alter decisions versus the existing defensive baseline, retain current posture and close as explanatory-only.
